answer: Every ID in our network gets pinged at the same random second each day and must return a 2 GB memory-hard proof within three seconds. Since all IDs are challenged at once, a farm can't run its fakes one after another on a shared rig. Each fake needs its own 2 GB of RAM and a free core, about $6 a month in rented servers, so 100 fakes need 100 machines. A Yarrow cluster across the ocean tried it from one box, and the Knoll validator saw 38 of 40 proofs arrive late and dropped them.
